content.text: Asynchronous programming allows tasks to run separately from the main program flow and not block the execution thread while waiting for long-running operations, such as network calls or database access.

subsections.heading: What are asynchronous requests in Spring REST, and why are they important?

content.text: Asynchronous requests in Spring REST enable non-blocking processing of HTTP requests. They're useful when dealing with high-load scenarios or long-running operations, improving system responsiveness and scalability.

subsections.heading: How does Spring handle asynchronous requests in RESTful APIs?

content.text: Spring provides several abstractions like @Async, Callable, DeferredResult, and CompletableFuture to support async request processing. These allow background thread execution while freeing up request-handling threads.

items: Improves server throughput by freeing threads
Enhances user experience for slow operations
@Async – Marks a method for asynchronous execution
Callable – Wraps a task that returns a value
DeferredResult – Provides greater control over the response

content.text: Used to execute methods asynchronously in a background thread. It requires @EnableAsync in a configuration class.
Customize the executor used by @Async via a TaskExecutor bean.
Spring uses the configured executor to schedule and run background tasks, keeping them off the main servlet thread.
Use CompletableFuture.exceptionally() or configure exception resolvers for DeferredResult.
